abstract: OECD analysis of 55.5 million online job postings from Canada, UK, and US (2018-2023) examining how digital technologies and AI are reshaping demand for skills in health occupations. Finds most health roles will be augmented rather than automated, with only a small fraction facing high automation risk.
keyFindings: 32% of health employment classified under potential augmentation by AI
4.3% of health roles (e.g. Pharmacy Technicians) identified as potentially automatable
0.6% of health workforce in high automation risk category (Orderlies, Medical Transcriptionists)
AI skills demand in healthcare job postings is 1.0%, below economy-wide average
Health Information Management demand increased from 24.0% to 25.1% of postings (2018-2023)
methodology: Analysis of 55.5 million online job postings from Canada, UK, and US between 2018-2023. Categorized health occupations by susceptibility to automation vs augmentation using GenAI and Advanced Robotics exposure frameworks.
qualifiers: Covers all health occupations, not limited to administrative roles. Automation potential does not equal actual displacement. Based on job posting analysis, not employer surveys or employment data.
